newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end slightly up on secondaries.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end slightly up on secondaries.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended slightly up on Monday on the back of active secondaries and a rise in heavyweight Telkom, but some profit-taking kept a cap on the index, brokers said.
They said overall market sentiment was quite firm with local investors dominating activity.

"I think the market on Tuesday will move in a narrow-range with the focus remaining on secondaries and retail counters. I don't expect any major rise or decrease in the index as we only have another five trading days this year," a broker from a Hongkong-based firm said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 0.55 points, or 0.09 percent, to close at 633.07 after touching 636.05 points.
Losers led gainers by 58 to 45, with 53 counters unchanged. Total volume was 116.4 million shares, boosted by cross-transactions in Telkom, while total turnover was 294 billion rupiah
Telkom recorded 11.5 million shares in cross-trade in what brokers said was part of a government placement of a block of 388 million shares from its stake in the state telecommunications giant.

Information technology and retail firm Multipolar topped the active list with 12.4 million shares traded, falling 150 rupiah to 1,525 rupiah on profit-taking after earlier reaching 1,750 rupiah, brokers said.
Brokers said some investors preferred to cash in their profits in Multipolar after their recent rise on speculation of an alliance with retailer Matahari.
Multipolar announced on Monday it had bought a 45-percent stake in PT Matahari Putra Prima and that it planned to buy an additional 5.1 percent.
Multipolar said that it would buy the 5.1 percent stake -- 23 million shares -- through a tender with an offer price of 3,200 rupiah per share.
Matahari rose 150 rupiah to 2,875 on a volume of 6.5 million shares on what brokers said was fresh buying.
Multipolar said the deal was designed to extend its retail access through Matahari's extensive chain of outlets through Indonesia
Analysts said market reaction was mixed, however.
"The market still needs time to analyse the impact of this deal on their bottom-line," one analyst with a London-Based firm said.
Telkom rose 50 rupiah to 4,225 on a volume of 2.3 million shares. Brokers said it was boosted by fresh buying after its higher New York Friday close of 35-1/8.
